57287-the-diary-of-a-french-private-war-.title: The Diary Of A French Private War Imprisonment 1914 1915
57287-the-diary-of-a-french-private-war-.creator: Unknown
57287-the-diary-of-a-french-private-war-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. _Gaston Riou was born on January 7, 1883. He is a native of the Cévennes, the region from which are derived three of the most distinguished among modern French psychologists, Melchior de Vogüé, Auguste Sabatier, and Paul Bourget. The Cévenole family from which he springs played an active part in the wars of religion.

arxiv-2108-13539.title: TOF-SIMS Analysis of Decoherence Sources in Nb Superconducting Resonators
arxiv-2108-13539.creator: Akshay A. Murthy 1, Jae-Yel Lee 1 , Cameron Kopas 2 , Matthew J. Reagor 2 , Anthony P. McFadden 3 , David P. Pappas 3 , Mattia Checchin 1 , Anna Grassellino 1 , Alexander Romanenko 1
arxiv-2108-13539.description: Abstract Superconducting qubits have emerged as a potentially foundational platform technology for addressing complex computational problems deemed intractable with classical computing. Despite recent advances enabling multiqubit designs that exhibit coherence lifetimes on the order of hundreds of μ \mu s, material quality and interfacial structures continue to curb device performance.

arxiv-2110-02893.title: On lattice width of lattice-free polyhedra and height of Hilbert bases
arxiv-2110-02893.creator: Martin Henk, Stefan Kuhlmann, Robert Weismantel
arxiv-2110-02893.description: Abstract Abstract. We study the lattice width of lattice-free polyhedra given by \bm{A}\bm{x}\leq\bm{b} in terms of \Delta(\bm{A}) , the maximal n\times n minor in absolute value of \bm{A}\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n} . Our main contribution is to link the lattice width of lattice-free polyhedra to the height of Hilbert bases and to the diameter of finite abelian groups.

arxiv-2201-02948.title: Tree-based Regression for Interval-valued Data
arxiv-2201-02948.creator: Chih-Ching Yeh, Yan Sun, Adele Cutler
arxiv-2201-02948.description: Abstract Regression methods for interval-valued data have been increasingly studied in recent years. As most of the existing works focus on linear models, it is important to note that many problems in practice are nonlinear in nature and therefore development of nonlinear regression tools for interval-valued data is crucial.

arxiv-2305-08239.title: Bayesian Flexible Modelling of Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Data
arxiv-2305-08239.creator: Arhit Chakrabarti, Yang Ni, Bani K. Mallick
arxiv-2305-08239.description: Abstract Single-cell RNA-sequencing technologies may provide valuable insights to the understanding of the composition of different cell types and their functions within a tissue. Recent technologies such as spatial transcriptomics , enable the measurement of gene expressions at the single cell level along with the spatial locations of these cells in the tissue.

arxiv-2504-12680.title: Embodied-R: Collaborative Framework for Activating Embodied Spatial Reasoning in Foundation Models via Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2504-12680.creator: Baining Zhao ∗ , Ziyou Wang ∗ , Jianjie Fang ∗ , Chen Gao † , Fanghang Man , Jinqiang Cui , Xin Wang , Xinlei Chen † , Yong Li , Wenwu Zhu Tsinghua University Project Page Code
arxiv-2504-12680.description: Abstract . Humans can perceive and reason about spatial relationships from sequential visual observations, such as egocentric video streams. However, how pretrained models acquire such abilities, especially high-level reasoning, remains unclear. This paper introduces Embodied-R, a collaborative framework combining large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for perception and small-scale Language Models (LMs) for reasoning.

arxiv-2601-00960.title: GA-NIFS: AGN activity in a Ly α \alpha emitter within a triple-AGN system anchored by a passive galaxy at z = 3 z=3
arxiv-2601-00960.creator: Michele Perna, Santiago Arribas, Mahmoud Hamed, Francesco D’Eugenio, Andrew J. Bunker, Stefano Carniani, Stéphane Charlot, Roberto Maiolino, Bruno Rodríguez Del Pino, Hannah Übler, Torsten Böker, Elena Bertola, Giovanni Cresci, Isabella Lamperti, Giacomo Venturi, Michele Ginolfi, Montserrat Villar M
arxiv-2601-00960.description: Abstract Context. Massive quenched galaxies at z > 3 z>3 challenge models of early galaxy evolution, as their rapid formation and abrupt quenching require efficient feedback, often linked to active galactic nuclei (AGN). The quiescent galaxy GS10578 at z = 3.064 z=3.064 is a key example of this population.

pmc-11643644.title: From Chains to Arrays: Substrate-Mediated Self-Assembly of Diboron Molecules
pmc-11643644.creator: Xiaoyu Hao, Huixia Yang, Mengmeng Niu, Tingting Wang, Hongyan Ji, Iulia Emilia Brumboiu, Cesare Grazioli, Ambra Guarnaccio, Albano Cossaro, Yan Li, Jingsi Qiao, Quanzhen Zhang, Liwei Liu, Teng Zhang, Yeliang Wang, Antonino Gulino, Erik K Hobbie
pmc-11643644.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this study, we explore the substrate-mediated control of self-assembly behavior in diboron molecules (C12H8B2O4, B2Cat2) using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The structural transformation of B2Cat2 molecules from one-dimensional (1D) molecular chains to two-dimensional (2D) molecular arrays was achieved by changing the substrate from Au(111) to bilayer graphene (BLG), highlighting the key role of substrate interactions in determining the assembly structure.

pmc-11678541.title: Dulaglutide and Dapagliflozin Combination Concurrently Improves the Endothelial Glycocalyx and Vascular and Myocardial Function in Patients with T2DM and Albuminuria vs. DPP-4i
pmc-11678541.creator: Emmanouil Korakas, John Thymis, Evangelos Oikonomou, Konstantinos Mourouzis, Aikaterini Kountouri, Loukia Pliouta, Sotirios Pililis, George Pavlidis, Stamatios Lampsas, Konstantinos Katogiannis, Lina Palaiodimou, Georgios Tsivgoulis, Gerasimos Siasos, Ignatios Ikonomidis, Athanasios Raptis, Vaia Lam
pmc-11678541.description: Background: The association between diabetic nephropathy and arterial elasticity and endothelial function is well established. In this study, we compared the effect of the combination of dulaglutide and dapagliflozin versus DPP-4 inhibitors on the endothelial glycocalyx, arterial stiffness, myocardial function, and albuminuria.

pmc-11802344.title: Advances in PIWI-piRNA function in female reproduction in mammals
pmc-11802344.creator: Xiaolong Lv, Hongdao Zhang, Ligang Wu
pmc-11802344.description: PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), which associate with PIWI clade Argonaute proteins to form piRNA-induced silencing complexes (piRISCs) in germline cells, are responsible for maintaining genomic integrity and reproductive function through transcriptional or post-transcriptional suppression of transposable elements and regulation of protein-coding genes.

pmc-12519609.title: Mental healthcare practices from entry to release across Southeastern jails
pmc-12519609.creator: Elena A DiRosa, Tonya Van Deinse, Gary S Cuddeback, Andrea Murray-Lichtman, Jessica Carda-Auten, David L Rosen
pmc-12519609.description: BackgroundIndividuals with mental illnesses are disproportionately incarcerated in jails, which have become de facto mental health institutions across the US. Yet there is limited research describing mental healthcare practices from entry to release among multiple jails and states.MethodsWe conducted 34 semi-structured interviews with jail healthcare personnel across five Southeastern states and used the Framework Method to guide analyses.

pmc-12645722.title: Correlation between aging, periodontal diagnoses and systemic diseases: a retrospective analysis of 3,000 patients
pmc-12645722.creator: Sukran Acipinar, Merve Yalcin
pmc-12645722.description: ObjectiveAging is a complex biological process driven by interconnected mechanisms such as inflammaging and immunosenescence. It serves as a significant risk factor for numerous chronic conditions. With increasing life expectancy, understanding the interplay between aging, systemic inflammation, and periodontitis has gained renewed research interest.

pmc-12652380.title: Exploring Emotional Self-Efficacy as a Mediator of Positive Leisure Experience and Subjective Well-Being Among Elementary School-Age Children in a Marginalized Community
pmc-12652380.creator: Mei-Ling Lin
pmc-12652380.description: Background: Prior research has established a positive relationship between emotional self-efficacy and life satisfaction in elementary school-age children. However, less is known about the direct impact of positive leisure experience on subjective well-being and the potential mediating role of emotional self-efficacy.

pmc-13425954.title: Cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity according to the ESC definition in patients receiving CAR T-cell therapy
pmc-13425954.creator: Jakob Christoph Voran, Carolin Richard, Astrid Dempfle, Christiane Pott, Philipp Nakov, Guranda Chitadze, Natalie Schub, Catrin Meyer, Hatim Seoudy, Derk Frank, Claudia D Baldus, Oliver J Müller, David Baden
pmc-13425954.description: BackgroundChimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has substantially improved outcomes in refractory hematologic malignancies but may cause cardiovascular complications, particularly in the context of cytokine release syndrome (CRS). Real-world data on incidence, severity, and prognostic relevance of cancer therapy–related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) defined by the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guidelines remain in the context of CAR-T cell therapy limited.

pmc-13643981.title: Predicting nurses’ behavioral intention to adopt artificial intelligence in a resource-limited setting: an extended technology acceptance model study in Iran
pmc-13643981.creator: Somaye Sohrabi, Hossein Bonakchi, Rahman Kazemi
pmc-13643981.description: BackgroundThe integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into healthcare systems has the potential to substantially enhance clinical decision-making, workflow efficiency, and quality of patient care. However, the successful implementation of AI technologies largely depends on their acceptance by frontline healthcare providers, particularly nurses.

pmc-13668649.title: Emergence of a Bundibugyo virus variant in the 2026 outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda
pmc-13668649.creator: Adrienne Amuri-Aziza, Gradi Luakanda-Ndelemo, Alisen Ayitewala, Daan Jansen, Pascal Adroba-Tandele, Andrew Nsawotebba, Eddy Kinganda-Lusamaki, Stephen Kanyerezi, Pontiano Kaleebu, Christian Ngandu, Allan Muruta, Daudi Jjingo, Susan Nabadda, Raphael Lumembe-Numbi, Olga Ntumba-Tshitenge, Misaki Wayeng
pmc-13668649.description: In May 2026, an outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV, species Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) was declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with cases originating from the DRC and locally transmitted cases reported in Uganda. Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreaks were previously recorded in 2007–2008 in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, and in 2012 in Isiro, DRC.
